title: Commodity intelligence and its engineered environment
claim: *Commodity intelligence and the governed engineering environment.* Training develops general-purpose capabilities; the harness turns reasoning into action. The engineer maintains the system knowledge and mechanisms that guide the agent, constrain its actions, and evaluate whether selected results may be accepted. Training data need not all be public.
purpose: Distinguish capability acquisition from agent operation and identify the engineer's principal locus of control.

topology.description: Three regions preserve capability acquisition, agent operation, and the Governed Engineering Environment. Training stages connect left to right; trained weights enter the deployed foundation model. Actions and changes flow downward to the existing system. Guidance flows upward to influence reasoning. Governance targets a perpendicular control mark at the actions-and-changes boundary. The engineer maintains the GEE and can optionally affect the pretraining/post-training process.

relations.solid: Directed causation, agent action, guidance, or engineering maintenance; the governance connector targets the action boundary.
relations.dashed: Optional training or fine-tuning, when feasible.

alt: Training data leads through pretraining and post-training to trained foundation-model weights. A deployed model provides four properties, each paired with an engineering implication, while the harness supplies tool action, context management, interposition and parallel execution. The agent changes an existing system. Guidance supplies system knowledge to the agent. Governance connects to the actions-and-changes boundary, constraining actions and controlling acceptance of selected results. The Governed Engineering Environment (GEE) contains the existing system and engineering structure. The engineer maintains this environment; an optional dashed training or fine-tuning route enters the pretraining and post-training process.
bw_encoding: 5% black fill identifies the model-development and environment regions; the heavier environment border identifies the engineer's principal sphere of control. Components and ordinary nodes are white. Text is black. Only the optional training relation is dashed and lightened.
typography: Bundled Source Sans 3; 11.5 pt region headings, 10.8 pt component headings, 10–10.5 pt ordinary labels, 9.5 pt relation and column annotations. Bold names regions/components; italic annotations distinguish the property/implication column roles and the system being changed. No shrink-to-fit. Web SVG realizes the same geometry at 2.25× coordinates with 21.375–25.875 CSS px labels; its 1003.5px natural width clamps legibly to the web column.
routing: Orthogonal connectors only. The optional dashed route enters Pretraining and post-training from the clear upper port; it no longer terminates at the outer model-development border or trained weights. Guidance retains its own upward arrow to agentic work. Governance uses a separate middle port and a leftward turn to a perpendicular control mark across Actions and changes. Swapping only the two gap channels avoids any governance/guidance crossing. All existing boxes and property rows retain their coordinates.
redesign: Retain the three-region composition and all four property/implication pairs. Redirect optional training/fine-tuning to the training process; name the Governed Engineering Environment (GEE); make governance constrain the actions-and-changes boundary instead of appearing as another input to the reasoner.
